nodes.name: High-temperature carburization
nodes.procedure: After the next high-temperature treatment under an Ar atmosphere at 900°C, the tungstate and Ru ions were reduced by the dopamine-derived carbon and further carburized to form tungsten carbide with anchored Ru single atoms (denoted as Ru SAs/WCx). Thermogravimetric analysis (TGA) indicates that stable and complete formation of tungsten carbide requires a heating temperature of above 830°C. X-ray diffraction (XRD) patterns and high-resolution transmission electron microscopy (HRTEM) also demonstrate that good crystallinity of WCx can be obtained at the optimal temperature of 900°C.

nodes.characterization_summary: HAADF-STEM shows nanocrystals with 0.251 nm interplanar spacing corresponding to WC (100) crystal plane; no Ru nanoparticles or clusters observed.
nodes.evidence_snippet: High-angle annular dark-field scanning transmission electron microscopy (HAADF-STEM) shows that nanocrystals appear with 0.251 nm interplanar spacing corresponding to the WC (100) crystal plane (Figure 1b), in which Ru nanoparticles and clusters are not observed.

properties.description: High-angle annular dark-field scanning TEM, panel (g)

nodes.characterization_summary: EDX elemental mapping indicates surface Ru content of 1.6 wt%.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The energy-dispersive X-ray (EDX) elemental mapping indicates that the surface Ru content is 1.6 wt% (Figure S7).

nodes.characterization_summary: ICP-AES indicates Ru content in the structure is 1.26 wt%.
nodes.evidence_snippet: inductively coupled plasma atomic emission spectroscopy (ICP-AES) indicates that Ru content in this structure is 1.26 wt% (Table S1).

nodes.characterization_summary: XRD pattern demonstrates Ru SAs/WCx consists of WC and W₂C crystalline phases without obvious diffraction peaks of Ru.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The XRD pattern (Figure 1h) demonstrates that Ru SAs/WCx consists of WC and W₂C crystalline phases without obvious diffraction peaks of Ru.

nodes.characterization_summary: XANES of Ru K-edge shows absorption threshold of Ru SAs/WCx close to Ru foil and lower than RuO₂, indicating average valence state close to metallic Ru.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The X-ray absorption near edge structure (XANES) of Ru K-edge shows that the absorption threshold of Ru SAs/WCx is close to that of Ru foil and lower than that of RuO₂ (Figure 1i).

nodes.characterization_summary: EXAFS spectra in R-space show one dominant coordination peak at 1.51 Å attributed to Ru-C bonds rather than Ru-Ru bonds.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The Fourier transform extended X-ray absorption fine structure (EXAFS) spectra in R-space show only one dominant coordination peak around 1.51 Å attributed to the Ru-C bonds rather than Ru-Ru bonds (Figure 1j).

properties.description: Normalized XRD or scattering data, panel (j)

nodes.characterization_summary: XPS of W₄f in Ru SAs/WCx shows peaks at 31.9 and 34.1 eV (W-C) and 36.1, 38.2 eV (W-O); introduction of Ru causes W-C peaks to shift to higher binding energy indicating electron transfer from W to Ru.
nodes.evidence_snippet: X-ray photoelectron spectroscopy (XPS) of W₄f in WCx samples shows the existence of peaks at 31.9 and 34.1 eV assigned to W-C bonds and higher binding energy peaks at 36.1 and 38.2 eV associated with W-O bonds of surface oxidation (Figure S9). The introduction of Ru atoms causes W-C bond peaks to have a slight shift to high binding energy, implying electron transfer from W to Ru and increased oxidation state of W compared with WCx.

nodes.characterization_summary: Electrochemical double-layer capacitance (Cdl) value of Ru SAs/WCx is 55.6 mF·cm⁻² indicating high exposure of active centers.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The electrochemical double-layer capacitance (Cdl) value of Ru SAs/WCx (55.6 mF·cm⁻²) indicates high exposure of active centers for HER.

nodes.characterization_summary: Charge transfer resistance of Ru SAs/WCx is 7 Ω reflecting reduced hindrances in charge transfer.
nodes.evidence_snippet: the smaller charge transfer resistance of 7 Ω of Ru SAs/WCx reflects reduced hindrances in the charge transfer between H₂O and electrocatalyst (Figure S14).
